title: Whole Chin Frame Table and Opposed Stools Preparation
description: One empty static optical-apparatus preparation display, one scene and zero new independent models. A whole existing chin/forehead-frame and binocular-column tabletop instrument stands toward the left of one complete open worktable. Its original independent frame, observation branch and illumination branch are retained. One entire empty trial-spectacle frame lies separately on the right tabletop, with real space between the two complete instruments. Two whole existing three-legged ring-footrest stools occupy opposite sides of the table, aligned with the main instrument but separated from its front and rear by visible empty floor intervals. These remain the original barstool forms, not claimed medical seating or anatomically fitted positions. Four distinct complete qualified old models form five unit-scale whole instances; each original geometry buffer, local normal, PBR dictionary and internal hierarchy is preserved. Only whole translations, one exact quarter turn of the small trial frame, and a finite ground slab are new. Unlike the old single-sided microscope-and-vials corner or the raised rear datum plate with two measuring stands and front caliper, this is a two-sided instrument-table station with separate whole stools and a clear side placement for the empty frame. No existing leg, headrest, lens rim, table brace or stool ring is removed, recoloured, resized or counted anew. No patient, real lens, illumination, diagnosis, vision testing, calibrated alignment, examination procedure, human fit, clinical workflow, medical suitability, load or workplace safety is made or verified. Rigging animation interaction not made.
